NULL (default) means bad control , case didbc reduces plain covariates. Multiple bad controls yet supported. xformula One-sided formula general exogenous covariates, entered pre-treatment-period level (default ~1) d_covs_formula One-sided formula general exogenous covariates, entered change (post minus pre) rather level. Default NULL (unused). bad_control_cov_formula One-sided formula auxiliary covariates (W paper) used model bad control's counterfactual evolution, entered pre-treatment-period level. variable name can used , including outcome (e.g. ~Y reproduces old "lagged outcome W" behavior). Default NULL (unused, ignored bad_control_formula NULL). bad_control_d_cov_formula Like bad_control_cov_formula, entered change (post minus pre) rather level. Covariate Unconfoundedness bad control given pre-period level (W, Z), "", .e. parallel trends bad control given (W, Z) (app:bad-control-parallel-trends supplementary appendix). "" supported est_method = "imputation", requires bad_control_formula non-NULL, distinguish binary bad control. nuisance_method est_method = "dr_ml" : "ml" (default) estimates doubly robust estimator's nuisance functions via cross-fitted random forests; "parametric" estimates via OLS/logistic regression, assuming correct specification. Ignored est_method = "imputation". control_group units serve controls: "notyettreated" (default) "nevertreated". Passed ptetools::two_by_two_subset. anticipation Number periods treatment can already affect outcome (default 0). Passed ptetools::two_by_two_subset. base_period pre-period compare post-period : "varying" (default) "universal". Passed ptetools::two_by_two_subset. weightsname Name sampling-weights variable data (default NULL) cband Logical; compute uniform confidence band instead pointwise confidence intervals (default TRUE) alp Significance level (default 0.05) boot_type "multiplier" (default) "empirical" bstrap Logical; whether use multiplier bootstrap (TRUE, default) purely analytical standard errors (FALSE) estimator returns influence function. bstrap = FALSE supports pointwise confidence intervals. cl Number clusters parallel computing bootstrap (default 1) biters Number bootstrap iterations (default 100) nfolds Number cross-fitting folds DR/ML (default 5) overlap_threshold est_method = "dr_ml" : unit's fitted propensity (preliminary, non-cross-fit fit) exceeds value (g,t) cell, estimation falls back imputation estimator cell, warning naming group, time period, offending unit IDs. Default 0.99. min_group_size est_method = "dr_ml" : (g,t) cell fewer treated units number propensity-score covariates plus min_group_size, estimation falls back imputation estimator cell, warning naming group, time period, treated count – separate trigger overlap_threshold, since fitting propensity score needs nontrivial treated sample identify , relative many covariates fit, can fail even good covariate overlap. Default 5, matching 's convention analogous check. num_threads est_method = "dr_ml", nuisance_method = "ml" : number threads grf's forests. Default NULL uses grf's auto-detection (available cores). Set 1 pin single thread per forest – e.g. Monte Carlo work, many reps run outer parallelism (one core ) rather letting individual forest fit claim every core machine. ... title: Estimate ATT(g,t) with Bad Controls — didbc
text: function implements methods Caetano, Callaway, Payne, Sant'Anna (2026). Two estimation approaches available: Imputation (est_method = "imputation"): Among controls, learn X_t ~ f(X(t-1), W, Z) treated, predict counterfactual X_t(0) Run using imputed X_t(0) instead observed X_t Doubly Robust ML (est_method = "dr_ml"): Estimate four nuisance functions via random forests Combine doubly robust score cross-fitting Returns influence function fast inference Requires grf package. Consistent either outcome regression propensity score correctly specified.
